Radiologists
RAD-01
Evaluate patients through diagnostic imaging and communicate findings

Determine a clinically usable image-based assessment by relating the clinical question and patient history to diagnostically adequate imaging, interpreting the examination, documenting the findings, and coordinating or communicating the result to the clinicians, patients, or families who use it.
A clinically usable imaging assessment is documented and available to those responsible for the patient’s care.
primary_output
broad

This is the broadly shared, high-relevance occupational outcome in the inventory. The included tasks form one substantive responsibility: obtain the relevant clinical context, ensure the examination can answer the question, interpret the images, and deliver a usable diagnostic assessment. Separate rows for PACS use, reports, consultation, and result communication describe components or delivery forms of that outcome rather than independent occupational outcomes.

Includes diagnostic interpretation across modalities, including diagnostic PET and nuclear cardiology, and case-level direction or approval needed for a diagnostically adequate examination. Includes communication only when it conveys or clarifies diagnostic findings. Excludes invasive image-guided procedures, radionuclide-specific planning or administration, treatment-plan ownership, system-level quality governance, and procedural consent or complication management.

Transactional, estate, and fiduciary practice

O*NET 30.3 includes Core tasks for drafting legal instruments and negotiating contracts, plus Supplemental probate and fiduciary tasks; reported titles include Contracts Attorney, Corporate Attorney, Estate Conservator, Real Estate Attorney, and Real Estate Lawyer.

Legal instruments, negotiated agreements, ownership determinations, probate matters, and fiduciary roles create or administer enforceable arrangements rather than merely advising about law or advocating a dispute. Their different subjects are merged because they share one separately assignable legal-arrangement outcome.

Includes drafting and reviewing nonlitigation legal instruments, contractual negotiation, public-record research used to establish ownership, probate and executor or administrator representation, and service as agent, trustee, guardian, or executor. Excludes general advice that does not create or administer an arrangement, settlement of an active dispute, litigation filings or advocacy, and legislation or government enforcement frameworks.
